answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil swarms with a drift-chart waypoint bond: each new identity must wander a proven route, earning standing waypoint by waypoint. Step one, it locks a 50 POA bond for 14 days. Step two, it finishes a paid task signed off by an unrelated peer. Step three, three receipts from three different peers unlock trading rights. A thousand clones would cost 50,000 POA locked plus 3,000 tasks, about 6,000 hours of work. An island of honest agents stays open only to those who sailed the route; clones wait outside the harbor like paper boats that never learned the tide.
